lines.text: This QR code is torn. And it still works.
See these three big squares? They tell your phone where the corners are, so it reads the code from any angle.
Every tiny block is one bit. Black is a one. White is a zero.
But a big part of the code isn't your data at all. It's backup.
A bit of maths called Reed–Solomon lets your phone use those extra blocks to rebuild the missing pieces.
At the highest level, up to 30% of the code can be gone.
It was invented in Japan in 1994, to track car parts in factories.
Save this, and send it to the friend whose shop QR is falling apart. Because now you know.
